name: Game board: era panels on a timeline
when: The voice walks from one game to the next on the same things (GTA IV's helicopter, bike and boat, then GTA V's): the first game's year and logo with a row of photo cards named underneath, then the board pans along a timeline to the second game, whose same things are already in place. Best when the order in time matters (the older game first).
anchor: at1, at2, at3: the first game's cards land on the words that name each thing; `next`: the board pans to the second game (on its name). The scene ends 0.23 s after `out`.
placement: Full screen on the video's ground: mount the clean ground (ground-B, or the darker ground-F or ground-G: one for the whole video) or ground-A (vice) under it with the same --start and the same length. Cut into it and out of it.

vars.theme: clean (on ground-B, white text, white card frames) or vice (on ground-A, ink text, gradient card frames): the video's theme
vars.game1: the first game, as logos.json names it (Grand Theft Auto IV); game2 the second
vars.logo1: its logo file: filled from assets/logos/ by build_video.mjs when game1 is listed there; logo2 the same. A logo is never drawn or invented
vars.year1: its release year (2008), shown with its logo; empty = none. year2 the same
vars.thing1: the first thing both games are compared on, one or two words (Helicopter); thing2 and thing3 the next ones
vars.a1: the first game's photo of thing1: each photo is a still of that game's own footage showing that thing, 16:9, cut with ffmpeg -ss T -i <shot> -frames:v 1 -vf "crop=<w>:<h>:<x>:<y>,scale=1280:720:flags=lanczos" -q:v 2 a1.jpg (the thing is the subject: big, whole, sharp, lit, not behind a character, no trailer text over it; crop so it fills most of the card). A thing with no clear still in one of the two games is left out of the board (the owner, 17 Nov 2026: skip what is too precise to source), never filled with another game's still or a drawing. a2, a3 the first game's next things; b1 to b3 the second game's
vars.thing3: the third thing (all three are needed: the row is laid out for three cards)
vars.at1: seconds after the start: the first game's first card lands (0.6); at2, at3 the next ones
vars.next: seconds after the start: the board pans to the second game (3.4), at least 0.5 s after the last card; the pan takes 0.5 s
vars.out: seconds after the start: everything fades out together (6.0); hold at least 1 s after the pan

source: new, built in the skills repo (owner, 17 Nov 2026)
